The problem with the Thermian argument is that it holds all creators to the standards of an individual. Any individual. Well, you could, free speech and all that, but the creator doesn't have to listen to you.

The first problem I have with this whole social justice movement is there's very little creating happening on their behalf. They will tear anything down that does not fit their criteria to a tee, but they offer no creations of their own that meet this almost impossible standard. instead of holding up examples of what is done well, they focus negatively on what they don't like.

The second problem I have is that social justice seems determined to remove anything that makes them, not just uncomfortable, but which they personally do not like. The problem with this is two-fold:

One, if you only ever surround yourself with things you already like you will never find anything new that you might also like, and create the kind of monotone existence that contradicts the constant cries for diversity (more on this in a moment)

Two, if you do not allow yourself to feel uncomfortable and deal with that, and overcome it, you're limiting your potential to grow. The idea that chains should be made illegal, instead of us having the power to break our own chains and empower ourselves.

Regarding diversity, I see a lot of clamour for more diversity, but that diversity seems limited to skin colour and gender quotas. There is no call for diversity of ideas, in fact there's quite the opposite. There is a demand for conformity and groupthink, the exact opposite of diversity, within the social justice movement.
